rubrics.justification: The response overstates what is visible in this single image, asserting a clearly defined eccentric ICM, circumferential cohesive TE, intact round architecture, and thinning zona that are not convincingly discernible. It largely repeats the provided Gardner grade rather than image-grounded morphology.

It integrates age, BMI, DOR, oocyte yield, endometrial thickness, prior cycle history, and semen parameters into prognosis reasonably well, though some links are overstated and AMH absence limits certainty.

The structure is logical overall, but several adjustments are weakly supported or speculative, such as penalizing moderate alcohol use and borderline motility for implantation, and inferring details like trilaminar endometrium or freeze-all considerations.

Single embryo transfer for a good-quality day-5 blastocyst at age 33 is guideline-concordant, but recommending PGT-A strongly for DOR after one failed transfer and suggesting adjunct testing/supplements without clear indication is more debatable than guideline-based.

The recommendations are clear and practical for transfer planning and contingency planning, including SET and routine optimization steps, though some suggested tests/interventions are not strictly necessary in this straightforward first-cycle case.
